clue.text: Man, say, finding small coin in garden

indicators.note: the coin sits in the garden, so its letters go inside the garden word

parts.note: a garden bed, a plot of flowers
1p, the one-penny piece, the smallest British coin, written I P

explanation.surface: Someone digging finds a tiny coin among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1p coin is written with the numeral read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A man is an example of a two-legged animal, and 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Prisoner is late getting some chocolate

parts.note: behind means late, behind schedule
chocolate comes in bars

explanation.surface: A prisoner is late collecting some chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind bars is the idiom for being imprisoned, as a prisoner is.

clue.text: Hull school

definitions.meaning: the outer casing of seeds such as peas
a group of whales or dolphins

explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a seed case, and also a group of whales.

clue.text: Foreign film may be given accolade

definitions.meaning: given a soundtrack in another language
knighted with a touch of the sword

explanation.definitionFit: Films get new soundtracks in translation, and a knight is tapped with a sword.

clue.text: Remarkable aspect now seen from penthouse window?

indicators.note: read as re-markable, able to be marked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: From a top-floor flat you get a remarkable new view.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ASPECT NOW gives the answer; the definition is a cryptic hint at an urban view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view of a town's buildings and streets is what you would see looking out from a high flat.

clue.text: Most reliable bonds held by financial controllers?

indicators.note: the bonds are held inside the controllers' word

parts.note: a trust is a body controlling money for others
ties are bonds or links

explanation.surface: The safest bonds are those held by bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trustiest is the superlative of trusty, meaning reliable.

clue.text: The measure of one across?

parts.note: the distance from one side to the other is a measure across

explanation.definitionFit: Width is the measurement of something from side to side.

clue.text: Signal for stopping work

definitions.meaning: the adjective meaning notable or remarkable

explanation.definitionFit: Striking means remarkable, and it is also walking out on strike.

clue.text: Venerable Scottish saint, his first name escaping monk

parts.note: august means venerable, revered

indicators.note: his first N for name runs away from the saint

parts.note: St Ninian was an early missionary saint of Scotland

explanation.surface: An old Scottish saint loses his first name and becomes a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his first ... escaping' takes the first N from NINIAN, leaving INIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Augustinian is a monk of the order following St Augustine's rule.

clue.text: Food for Cockney — does him good, he says?

indicators.note: the Cockney is speaking, so we write what he pronounces

parts.note: something that heals does him good

explanation.surface: A Cockney's favourite dish is good for his health.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their H, so 'heals' comes out as 'eels'; jellied eels are a traditional East London dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Jellied eels are a famous food of London's East End.

clue.text: Narrow end of blade secured by concealed spring

indicators.note: the blade's end is held fast between the two other pieces

parts.note: concealed means hid
to spring is to bound, leap

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word blade

explanation.surface: A thin blade's tip is held in place by a hidden spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound describes a narrow-minded person stuck in conventional views.

clue.text: Magnificent king's daughter finally got changed

indicators.note: the king's daughter's last letter is swapped for another one, which the definition settles

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A splendid princess finally undergoes a transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally got changed' says only that REGAN's last letter alters; the definition shows the N becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, fit for a monarch, hence splendid or magnificent.

clue.text: Unimportant event low on Richter scale?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something not much good or of little note
read literally, a minor tremor is not a great shaking of the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mediocre, nothing special, while literally it describes small tremors.

clue.text: Honest John's account?

parts.note: the evangelist John's book is a sacred narrative held to be wholly true

explanation.definitionFit: Gospel truth is something absolutely true, like the Gospels for believers.

clue.text: Travelled over both sides of lake to capture snail

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the next

parts.note: went means travelled

indicators.note: both sides of lake picks its first and last letters

parts.note: to trap is to capture

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses a lake to catch a snail.
explanation.definitionFit: The wentletrap is a sea snail with a spiralling ridged shell.

clue.text: Common mistake pronouncing 'poet's middle name

indicators.note: pronouncing tells us to say the name and write what is heard

parts.note: Percy Bysshe Shelley, the Romantic poet, had Bysshe as his middle name

explanation.surface: Someone often gets a poet's middle name wrong when saying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bish is British slang for a blunder or error.

clue.text: Commercial mail centre processing letters

indicators.note: the letters of mail centre are processed, run through and rearranged

explanation.surface: A postal sorting office is busy dealing with commercial post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to merchants and trade, so commercial.

clue.text: Narrow decision to make visit to dean and chapter?

parts.note: a dean and chapter live in a cathedral close
to call is to visit

explanation.surface: A tight vote over whether to visit the cathedral clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is a narrowly decided matter or a near miss.

clue.text: Stock this sort of clothing

parts.note: stock is a wide band worn round the throat, not a shop's goods

explanation.definitionFit: A stock is a cravat, a kind of garment worn at the throat.

clue.text: Group head off after country dance, taking seats again

indicators.note: the group word follows the dance word

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish country dance

indicators.note: the first letter of the group word is removed

parts.note: a section is a group or division

explanation.surface: A team leaves after a dance at a country do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes S from SECTION, giving ECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-election is winning one's seat in parliament once more.

clue.text: Offering fruit — about time

indicators.note: about tells us the fruit is turned round

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

explanation.surface: A present of fruit arrives, and about time too.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something offered or presented, an offering.

clue.text: Most strenuous call for 6?

definitions.meaning: the union's cry for a strike, linking to the answer at 6

explanation.definitionFit: All-out means with full effort, and it is a union's demand for everyone to strike.

clue.text: Summon up courage to leave the board

definitions.meaning: an idiom for committing boldly to a risky decision
literally what a diver does, jumping off the diving board

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to commit boldly, and literally it is diving into water.

clue.text: Peak one's first to climb? That may be debatable

parts.note: a top is a peak
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of climb

explanation.surface: A climber's first summit invites argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject for debate or discussion.

clue.text: Country houses appear heartless to artist

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the houses' word

parts.note: halls are large country houses

explanation.surface: Stately homes seem cold to a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age portrait painter.

clue.text: Reflect a prior interest

indicators.note: prior means the letter a comes before the other piece

parts.note: to muse is to reflect or ponder

explanation.surface: Think about something you were once interested in.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to hold their interest or entertain them.

clue.text: Extremely eager to go on green course, seeing pollution?

indicators.note: the extreme letters of eager are added on after the course

parts.note: pea soup is a green first course of a meal

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of eager

explanation.surface: A keen golfer heads out onto a green course despite the smog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives ER, the first and last letters of 'eager'. A pea-souper is a thick yellow-green London fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense smoggy fog caused by air pollution.

clue.text: Dickens hero in a spot

definitions.meaning: the young protagonist of Great Expectations
a dot on dice or dominoes

explanation.definitionFit: Pip is the hero of Great Expectations, and a pip is a spot on a die.

clue.text: Circular considered from all viewpoints

definitions.meaning: round in shape, like a ball
an all-round view, looked at from every side

explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means round like a ball and, figuratively, viewed all round.

clue.text: Provide a little more drink, perhaps, for dog

definitions.text: Provide a little more drink, perhaps

parts.note: for can mean to, as in a present for or to someone
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Refill a glass, maybe, for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass is to refill it, a common way of providing more drink.
